name: Bisk Clay Studio

description: A cosy, roughly 30 x 30 ft family-run studio in the Upper Haight, offering memberships, six-week courses and one-night workshops with a music-loving community feel.

'Family Membership' includes 8am-10pm access, personal shelf, glazes; clay must be bought from the studio and its price includes glaze and firing fees; cone 5/6 midfire; kilns run 1-2 times a week. Membership via request form. Contact (847) 287-8880, unclepaulsceramics@gmail.com. Teaching lead: No hiring page. The studio runs a 'Featured Artist Series' of guest-taught workshops (Susan Gold teapot workshop, Oct 2026) and its team page lists working-artist instructors; a guest workshop pitch (e.g. wild clay or glaze chemistry) could be sent to unclepaulsceramics@gmail.com. description: West Oakland nonprofit fine and industrial arts school whose ceramics department teaches pinching, coiling, slabs, wheel throwing, press molds, slip casting, mid-fire glazing and raku, for adults and youth.

Best Glaze Practices workshop with Don Santos, Nov 14. Teaching lead: No instructor posting found. name: Colibri Pottery Studio
description: A minority woman-owned pottery studio with two San Jose locations (North San Jose and one by Campbell) and 23 wheels across both. It offers beginner wheel classes, 6-week courses and memberships.
details: Membership $220/month + $98 one-time initiation, 3-month minimum. Includes a shelf and members-only area with two bins, 23 wheels and 40+ glazes; clay at wholesale with $15 firing per 25 lb bag. Not for production potters. Requires wheel or handbuilding proficiency, or completing their 6-week course. Phones: North San Jose 408-592-6297, Campbell 408-593-4080. info@colibripotterystudio.com. Teaching lead: The jobs page lists open roles including 'Pottery Instructor' (also Studio Tech, Studio Manager and Art Intern). No pay is listed. Apply via the online form at https://www.colibripotterystudio.com/jobs, which asks for name, email, phone, roles, preferred studio, an optional portfolio link, and your 'experience with clay or teaching, availability, and why you'd like to join'. Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).
address: North San Jose: 1620 Oakland Rd, Suite D102, San Jose, CA 95131; 'Campbell' studio: 1033 S Bascom Ave, San Jose, CA 95128

name: Blossom Hill Ceramics
description: A long-running South Bay pottery school (55-year history, started in a Los Gatos garage) with 200+ artists, 40+ wheels, a dedicated handbuilding room, a porcelain studio, and mid and high fire kilns.
details: Open studio 7am-11pm, 365 days a year. Membership with an ongoing intermediate/advanced class is $355/month (3-month minimum); membership without a class is $296/month after 3 months. Membership includes all clay, glazes, firings and free workshops; locker +$10/month; porcelain studio $59/month after 3 months. 6-week handbuilding series $425 (members $120). teambhc@blossomhillcrafts.com, 408-202-7125. Teaching lead: The employment page lists a Studio Technician role (clay recycling, kiln loading, mixing glazes and slips) at $21-22/hour, 10-20 hrs/week, including a studio membership. Apply with a resume and three references to tasha@blossomhillcrafts.com (https://www.blossomhillcrafts.com/jobposting-studiotech.html). It is not a teaching post, but the ongoing classes are instructor-led, so a direct inquiry about teaching is reasonable.
address: 15900 Blossom Hill Rd, Los Gatos, CA (store: 354 East Campbell Avenue, Campbell)

name: Creative Crew Studio
description: A small Saratoga pottery studio run by Amita, offering wheel and hand-building experiences, workshops, members-only open studio and private events.
details: Pottery wheel experience $75; pottery painting from $35; DIY kits $45. Workshops are open to the public; open studio is for members only. Phone 408-505-4972.
address: 12175 Saratoga Sunnyvale Road, Suite C, Saratoga, CA 95070

image.alt: A row of students at pottery wheels in the Creative Crew Studio classroom

name: Art Space on the Coast
description: A community art studio in downtown Pacifica founded by local ceramic artist Jennifer Christiansen. It offers daily studio rental (4 wheels, slab roller), classes, and a firing service for work made elsewhere.
details: Daily studio space rental bookable online. Firing service (bisque, low and mid-range, electric): $0.07/cu in for bisque or low fire (cone 04/06), $0.10/cu in for mid-fire (cone 5/6), $10 minimum; cookies $2. Only commercial clays and glazes are accepted (no wild clay). The learning space can be rented for one-time events (up to 16) or a class series (8). Teaching lead: The studio hosts outside instructors: the learning space can be rented for a class series (capacity 8), so a short course could run here. Contact via the site. Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).

name: Art Beat Studio
description: A downtown Campbell art and pottery studio for kids, teens and adults, running a weekly beginner wheel 'Try it' night, camps and workshops.
details: Wheel experience: 2-hour lesson, your own wheel, up to 3 pieces (keep the best 2), 15 glaze colours, firing included, pickup in 3-4 weeks. Open studio $15 for 2 hours. Phone 408-370-5002; Instagram @the.art.beat; site www.artbeatstudio.co. 2026 activity is not confirmed: the evidence is a Downtown Campbell listing of weekly wheel nights through December 2025, and the studio site needs JavaScript.

name: Foster City Community Center Ceramics Studio
description: The new Foster City Community Center in Leo Ryan Park opened in September 2026 with a dedicated ceramics studio. It replaces the old Recreation Center pottery programme, whose members moved to Clayroom San Mateo during construction.
details: The city sought an outside operator for the ceramics studio (RFI, proposals due March 20, 2026) to run classes, workshops, camps and open studio. No operator is named on the pages I could open. Ribbon cutting and building dedication on Saturday, September 19, 2026. Contact: Tiffany Oren, Recreation Manager, (650) 286-3395; general line (650) 286-3380. Teaching lead: Feb 2026 release: 'the City is looking for enthusiastic individuals to serve as class instructors in the new facility. Those interested should provide qualifications, a proposed program approach, and submit a resume in the class instructors tab on the application website'. This is separate from the operator RFI and has no fixed deadline. The vendor application page URL in the release now returns 404, so contact the Recreation Manager directly, and ask who won the ceramics operator contract. Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).

name: Pacifica Community Center Ceramics
description: City of Pacifica ceramics sessions in the Community Center's ceramics room: a relaxed morning work session for people with basic clay experience.
details: Thursdays, Oct 1 - Dec 17, 2026; the next session is listed for Jan 7 - Mar 25, 2027. Listed for ages 50+. 'No major instructions given during class'; instructor George Bunea. Price shown at registration.

name: Southside Community Center Ceramics (San Jose PRNS)
description: San Jose Parks, Recreation and Neighborhood Services ceramics sessions at Southside Community Center, run year-round for older adults.
details: Tuesdays Nov 3 - Dec 15, 2026 (with earlier 2026 sessions also listed). Ages 50+. The instructor is listed as a PRNS Volunteer. Price at registration. Teaching lead: The instructor slot is a PRNS volunteer role. Volunteering with San Jose PRNS could be an easy first local teaching credit (ask Southside Community Center).

name: Heath Ceramics Sausalito Factory & Showroom
description: Heath's original 1959 dinnerware factory, where about 40 craftspeople still make the clay and form, glaze and fire every dinnerware piece. It has a showroom, seconds, an overstock tile shed and factory tours by RSVP.
details: Showroom and pickup Mon-Sun 10am-5pm; Overstock Tile Shed Mon-Sun 10am-4pm. Factory tours by advance RSVP. Phone 415 332 3732 x1. Approach via Harbor Drive because of the condition of Gate 5 Road. (The SF Alabama St factory is already on the map.) Teaching lead: Heath careers page (https://www.heathceramics.com/pages/careers) currently lists only a temporary accounting role, no clay studio or production openings. Worth watching; the Heath Clay Studio's master potters run public workshops.

image.alt: A table set with Heath Ceramics stoneware plates and bowls

name: Mt Vision Ceramics Studio (Jess Taylor)
description: Inverness potter and geophysicist Jess Taylor makes glazes and clay bodies from the local Mount Vision granite and clay, and publishes detailed glaze tests and firing schedules online.
details: Studio on the eastern slope of Mount Vision above Inverness, open during Point Reyes Open Studios. Contact info@mtvision.studio. The site has an organized series of granite-glaze articles (copper, controlled cooling, specific gravity). Teaching lead: Not a job lead, but a natural peer for wild-clay and glaze-chemistry work (local granite glazes). A possible collaboration or exchange contact via info@mtvision.studio.

image.alt: Two glazed cups with an amber glaze made at Mt. Vision Ceramics Studio

name: Joy Imai, Special Handling Pottery
description: Studio potter Joy Imai has thrown and hand-built porcelain in her studio and shop at the historic Allied Arts Guild since 1986. The shop also carries Japanese pottery and work by other artisans.
details: Winter hours: Nov 1-28, 2026 Wed-Sat 11:30am-3:30pm; Dec 1, 2026 to Mar 2027 open five days (closed Sun-Mon). Phone 650-321-8188.
address: Allied Arts Guild, 75 Arbor Road, Suite R, Menlo Park, CA 94025

name: Point Reyes Open Studios
description: Artist-run open studios held twice a year around Tomales Bay (Point Reyes Station, Inverness, Olema, Marshall), with about 25 members, ceramicists among them.
details: Studios open 11am-5pm, Saturday-Monday on Memorial Day weekend and Friday-Sunday on Thanksgiving weekend. Free and self-guided; map on the site.

image.alt: The main street of Point Reyes Station

name: Foothill College Ceramics
description: A community college ceramics emphasis within the Art AA and certificate, with a strong kiln setup and the Claybodies student club, which brings in visiting artists and runs an annual pottery sale.
details: 25 wheels; Geil DBL-30 downdraft gas kiln, Alpine 24 gas kiln, 4 Skutt 1224 electric kilns, 1 Paragon front-loader, 2 raku kilns and a catenary arch cross-draft soda kiln. Lead: Andy Ruble, rubleandy@fhda.edu. Teaching lead: Community college adjunct teaching goes through Foothill-De Anza district HR. Andy Ruble (ceramics lead) is the person to ask about adjunct pools or visiting-artist talks with Claybodies. Foothill-De Anza district posts part-time faculty pools (a district 'Studio Art Instructor' pool PT041 mentioning ceramics exists but its PDF could not be opened). CA minimum qualification for art is a Master's in fine arts (incl. ceramics), art or art history, or equivalency. Ask Andy Ruble about adjunct needs; district HR employment@fhda.edu.
address: 12345 El Monte Road, Los Altos Hills, CA 94022

image.alt: An instructor and a student with a vase on the wheel in a Foothill College ceramics class

name: College of San Mateo Ceramics
description: CSM's art department runs a ceramics lab within its 3D Art, Ceramics and Sculpture area, a low-cost way to get kiln and wheel access on the Peninsula.
details: Ceramics Lab Coordinator: Eric Elfving, elfvinge@smccd.edu, (650) 574-6290. Teaching lead: Adjunct hiring goes through the San Mateo County Community College District; contact the Ceramics Lab Coordinator about openings. San Mateo County CCD (CSM, Skyline, Canada) adjunct postings are on the SMCCD jobs site; none found for ceramics in this pass. Eric Elfving is the lab contact.
address: 1700 W. Hillsdale Boulevard, San Mateo, CA 94402

image.alt: The plaza on the College of San Mateo campus

name: Mission College Ceramics
description: Mission College's art programme has ceramics studios and repeatable Ceramics-Handbuilding (ART 065A-D) and Ceramics-Potter's Wheel (ART 067A-D) courses.
details: A new course rotation starts in the 2026-27 academic year; courses may be cancelled due to circumstances (contact the department). Teaching lead: Part-Time Ceramics Instructor (Pool), work location Mission College, posted 05/20/2025, open until filled, applications kept one year. Pay prorated from $38,464-$55,582/semester. This posting lists MQ as a bachelor's plus two years related professional experience, an associate's plus six years, a CA CC Instructor's Credential, or equivalent (lower bar than the usual art MQ, so worth checking). Apply online via the district (careers.insidehighered.com job 3418837 links to the application). Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).
address: 3000 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054

name: Creative Growth Art Center
description: The oldest and largest art centre for artists with developmental, mental and physical disabilities, where ceramics is one of the core studio disciplines; its 2025 show "Fired Up" surveyed clay work by studio artists.
details: Studio Program disciplines listed: drawing, painting, video production, ceramics, wood, fiber arts, textiles, printmaking. Saturday Youth Program also includes ceramics and runs year round. Phone 510.836.2340; general email gallery@creativegrowth.org. Teaching lead: Open Positions page (creativegrowth.org/open-positions) currently lists Studio Director and Studio Operations Manager (apply via the APPLY button, which opens a Google Drive job description). No ceramics facilitator role is posted right now; the studio uses a team of facilitators and has previously recruited substitute art facilitators, so worth contacting gallery@creativegrowth.org to ask about facilitator or substitute pools. Has a 'Join Our Team' page (https://www.creativegrowth.org/join-our-team) with an 'Open Positions' section; no specific roles were readable in the fetched page, so check it directly for studio or ceramics facilitator openings.

name: SFArtsED (San Francisco Arts Education Project)
description: Nonprofit that places professional artists in SF public schools for residencies, plus summer camps and after-school programs. Ceramics is listed among the visual arts disciplines they hire for.
details: Resident Artists are part-time employees; pay rises with experience (no rates stated). K-8 residencies run six weeks to a full school year; summer camp artists recruited late winter and spring; 'We interview all year for upcoming positions.' Teaching lead: Artist Disciplines include 'Visual Arts (Mixed media, Fine Arts, Ceramics, Textile)'. Apply via the application form on the Opportunities page, then email resume, cover letter, examples of professional work, work with students and a sample project proposal to Mia Waller, Program Director, mia.w@sfartsed.org (or mail to the Minnesota Street address). Selected artists get an interview and classroom audition. Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).

name: Root Division
description: Artist-run nonprofit with subsidized studios, a gallery and adult classes taught by its studio artists and alums, including an intro handbuilding course. Studio artists can choose teaching in the adult education program as their work-trade.
details: Ceramics Studio: Intro to Handbuilding with Tony Lopez-Romero, Mondays 6:30-8:30 PM, Jan 26-Feb 23 (2026 season), $385. Studio Artist program: subsidized studios 100-230 sq ft in exchange for 8 hours/month work-trade (teaching is one option); next deadline November 1, 2026 for February 2027 move-in; must tour studios (Tue/Thu) at least three months before applying; apply via SlideRoom. Note: the studios page does not list a kiln or ceramics as a suited discipline. Contact info@rootdivision.org, 415.863.7668. Teaching lead: Adult classes are 'Taught by our Studio Artists or Alums'. Becoming a Root Division Studio Artist (rootdivision.org/apply/apply-studio/) is the route to teaching there; teaching in adult education counts toward the 8-hour monthly work-trade. Root Division also runs teaching fellowships (Filipinx Teaching Artist Fellowship 2026-27 is closed; Education Fellowship paid a $4,000 stipend in 2025-26). Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).

name: De Anza College Ceramics
description: Large community college ceramics programme with a full ladder of wheel throwing (beginning to advanced) plus handbuilding, raku, decoration and low-fire courses.

CA MQ: Master's in fine arts/art/art history or equivalency.

description: Community college visual arts department with dedicated ceramics, painting and drawing studios and a bronze foundry. Its district runs an open part-time ceramics instructor pool.

MQ: Master's in fine arts (includes ceramics), art or art history; or Bachelor's in those plus Master's in humanities; or equivalent (submit equivalency form). Foreign transcripts need a course-by-course evaluation, relevant for non-US credentials. Paid teaching is US employment: it needs work authorization (the current visa doesn't allow it; an O-1B or a sponsoring employer could).

name: Cal State East Bay Art & Design (Ceramics)
description: CSU art department with ceramics, sculpture, printmaking and painting studios on the Hayward campus. It keeps an annual lecturer pool that explicitly covers ceramics.
details: Lecture Pool for Department of Art and Design (AY 26-27), job 557363, advertised April 23, 2026, open until filled. Appointments for Fall 2026 (starts Aug 17, 2026) and Spring 2027 (starts Jan 19, 2027). Lecturer ranges from $5,507 up to $15,211 (Range 2-5; hiring generally near the minimum). Department email artdept@csueastbay.edu. name: Walnut Creek Chili Bowl and Handcrafted Holiday Sale
description: Annual community events from the Walnut Creek arts school: a Chili Bowl fundraiser and a Handcrafted Holiday Sale of ceramics, prints and more by teaching artists and students.
details: Chili Bowl Fundraiser 11/14/2026, 11:00 AM; Handcrafted Holiday Sale 12/05/2026 (per home page upcoming events). Earlier listings put the sale at the Shadelands center, 111 N. Wiget Lane, free to attend.
address: Shadelands Art Center, 111 N. Wiget Lane, Walnut Creek

name: Renegade Craft Fair San Francisco
description: Big juried indie craft fair at Fort Mason, a common first market for Bay Area potters selling mugs and functional ware.
details: Fall/Winter: November 14 + 15, 2026 at Fort Mason Center Festival Pavilion. Spring fair listed March 28 + 29 at Fort Mason (indoors). Vendor costs on apply page: $35 nonrefundable application fee per event; 5x10 ft shared booth $400, 10x10 ft $800, 10x20 ft $2000. Each fair juried independently.
address: Fort Mason Center Festival Pavilion, San Francisco

image.alt: Crowds browsing the craft stalls at a Renegade Craft Fair in a large hall

name: Mill Valley Fall Arts Festival
description: Juried show of 135 fine art and fine craft artists under the redwoods, in its 69th year; production work is not allowed, so it suits one-off studio pottery.
details: 2026 festival Sept 19-20, 10am-5pm. 2026 call: 5 images, $45 application fee ($55 after April 15), deadline May 15, notification by May 22; booth fees tiered from $385; four $500 Awards of Excellence; artists must be present both days and hold a California resale permit. Applications via Zapplication. Expect a similar spring 2027 call.
address: Old Mill Park, Throckmorton Ave. & Cascade Drive, Mill Valley

image.alt: Festival-goers on the street under the Mill Valley Fall Arts Festival sign
image.credit: Image: Mill Valley Fall Arts Festival

name: Marin Open Studios
description: Two-weekend county-wide open studios in May where Marin artists, potters included, open their workspaces and sell directly.
details: 2026 dates: May 2-3 and May 9-10 (2025: May 3-4 and 10-11). Site has artist login, loan forms and a juried exhibit. Marin-wide event; San Rafael given only as a county reference city.

image.alt: An artist standing in her studio among landscape paintings, Marin Open Studios

name: East Bay Open Studios
description: Free open studios across ten East Bay cities, now run by Oakland Art Murmur, with a winter edition coming up just before the holidays.
details: Winter 2026: December 5-6 and 12-13, studios open 11am-5pm, 250+ artists across 10 East Bay cities, free. The spring 2026 edition ran June 6-7 and 13-14 with an opening at Orchard Galleries May 30. Site has 'Register for EBOS', an Artist Professional Development Series, and Space Requests & Fee Waivers.

image.alt: An artist painting at an easel in her studio, East Bay Open Studios

name: Silicon Valley Open Studios
description: Three May weekends of open studios from the coast and Peninsula to the South Bay, with ceramics among the featured media; 2026 was its 40th year with 370+ artists.
details: SVOS 2027: May 1-2 Coastside and Northern Peninsula; May 8-9 Mid-Peninsula; May 15-16 South Bay; 11am-5pm. Registration for exhibiting artists opens December 1 (Dec/Jan). Year-round SVVA membership $50 (directory listing, quarterly mixers and exhibitions, artist webinars). Region-wide; San Jose given as a reference city.

name: CCACA: California Conference for the Advancement of Ceramic Art
description: Annual ceramics conference founded by John Natsoulas and Robert Arneson, pairing lectures and demos by working ceramic artists with 50+ student exhibitions around downtown Davis. Outside the core Bay Area (about 75 miles) but the main regional clay conference, and Bay Area colleges take part.
details: CCACA 2027 presenters listed: Gerit Grim, Clayton Keyes, Kyungmin Park, George Rodriguez, Bonnie Seeman, George Grant & Eusebio Lozano. 2027 dates not stated on the page (the 2026 edition was in April). The gallery also hosts workshops.
address: John Natsoulas Gallery, 521 1st Street, Davis, CA

image.credit: Image: California Conference for the Advancement of Ceramic Art
